title: Topic 11 · सरकार, शासन व्यवस्था र सार्वजनिक खर्च
blocks: h2
Academic noun (१० वटा)
ul
**governance** (शासन व्यवस्था): Good governance depends on transparency and accountability.
**legislation** (कानुन बनाउने काम): New legislation was passed to curb pollution.
**bureaucracy** (कर्मचारीतन्त्र): Excessive bureaucracy slows down public services.
**subsidy** (अनुदान): Fuel subsidies keep transport affordable for the poor.
**taxation** (कर लगाउने प्रणाली): Progressive taxation redistributes wealth.
**accountability** (जवाफदेहिता): Voters demand greater accountability from officials.
**welfare** (जनकल्याण): The welfare system supports the unemployed.
**expenditure** (खर्च): Public expenditure on health has risen steadily.
**transparency** (पारदर्शिता): Transparency reduces the scope for corruption.
**policy** (नीति): Sound economic policy underpins stable growth.
h2
Precise verb (१० वटा) · past, participle, -ing रूप
ul
**allocate** (allocated, allocated, allocating): The budget allocates more to education this year.
**implement** (implemented, implemented, implementing): Governments must implement reforms carefully.
**regulate** (regulated, regulated, regulating): Agencies regulate food safety and drug quality.
**subsidise** (subsidised, subsidised, subsidising): The state subsidises public transport.
**legislate** (legislated, legislated, legislating): Parliament legislated against child labour.
**govern** (governed, governed, governing): A stable coalition now governs the country.
**impose** (imposed, imposed, imposing): The government imposed a tax on sugary drinks.
**prioritise** (prioritised, prioritised, prioritising): Officials must prioritise essential services.
**fund** (funded, funded, funding): The state fully funds primary schooling.
**reform** (reformed, reformed, reforming): The new minister pledged to reform the tax system.
h2
Collocation र adjective (१० वटा)
ul
**public spending**: Public spending on healthcare must rise. (Writing)
**tax revenue**: Tax revenue funds essential services. (Writing)
**welfare state**: The welfare state protects the most vulnerable. (Writing)
**government intervention**: Government intervention is sometimes unavoidable. (Writing)
**fiscal policy**: Sound fiscal policy controls inflation. (Writing)
**red tape**: Businesses complain about excessive red tape. (Speaking and Writing)
**accountable to the public**: Officials must remain accountable to the public. (Writing)
**public services**: Reliable public services improve daily life. (Speaking and Writing)
**state-funded**: State-funded universities widen access. (Writing)
**budget deficit**: A large budget deficit limits future spending. (Writing)
h2
Formal Task 2 collocation (५ वटा) · Writing
ul
**allocate resources to**: The government should allocate more resources to healthcare.
**prioritise public spending**: Authorities must prioritise public spending on essentials.
**hold the government accountable**: Free elections hold the government accountable.
**impose higher taxes**: One option is to impose higher taxes on the wealthy.
**invest in public services**: Investing in public services benefits everyone.
h2
Speaking idiom र expression (५ वटा) · Speaking-का लागि मात्र
ul
**throw money at**: Simply throwing money at a problem rarely solves it. (Part 3)
**tighten the purse strings**: In a downturn, the government tightens the purse strings. (Part 3)
**call the shots**: In the end, elected leaders should call the shots. (Part 3)
**for the greater good**: Some sacrifices are made for the greater good. (Part 3)
**cut through the red tape**: We need to cut through the red tape to speed things up. (Part 3)

blocks.title: Exercise 4.11.3 · Speaking अभ्यास (Simulation Drill)
blocks.instructions: Part 3-को प्रत्येक question-को उत्तर २ देखि ३ वटा वाक्यमा दिनुहोस्, र कम्तीमा एउटा target idiom र एउटा collocation प्रयोग गर्नुहोस्। त्यसपछि model answer-सँग दाँजेर हेर्नुहोस्।

items.prompt: What should governments spend most of their money on?
items.answer: Governments should prioritise public spending on essentials such as healthcare and education, since simply throwing money at less urgent projects rarely serves the greater good.

items.prompt: Do you think higher taxes on the wealthy are fair?
items.answer: I think they are fair, within reason; the wealthy can afford to contribute more, and that revenue can fund public services, though taxes should not be so high that they discourage enterprise.

items.prompt: How can governments reduce corruption and waste?
items.answer: Governments can curb corruption through greater transparency, strict accountability, and cutting through the red tape that gives officials room to abuse the system.

**fuel** (इन्धन): Higher fuel prices raise the cost of everything.
**emission** (उत्सर्जन): Vehicle emissions are a major source of urban pollution.
**congestion** (ट्राफिक जाम): Congestion charges aim to reduce city traffic.
**transit** (सार्वजनिक यातायात): A modern transit system eases pressure on roads.

**congest** (congested, congested, congesting): Private cars congest the narrow roads.
**navigate** (navigated, navigated, navigating): Cyclists navigate busy streets daily.
**emit** (emitted, emitted, emitting): Older buses emit far more pollution.
**relieve** (relieved, relieved, relieving): A new bypass relieved chronic congestion.

blocks.title: Exercise 4.12.3 · Speaking अभ्यास (Simulation Drill)
blocks.instructions: Part 3-को प्रत्येक question-को उत्तर २ देखि ३ वटा वाक्यमा दिनुहोस्, र कम्तीमा एउटा target idiom र एउटा collocation प्रयोग गर्नुहोस्। त्यसपछि model answer-सँग दाँजेर हेर्नुहोस्।

items.prompt: How can traffic congestion in big cities be reduced?
items.answer: Congestion can be eased by investing in mass transit and introducing congestion charges to discourage private car use; otherwise cities simply grind to a halt at rush hour.

items.prompt: Do you think people rely too much on private cars?
items.answer: More often than not, yes; many people reach for the car out of habit even for short trips, which leaves roads bumper to bumper and worsens emissions.

items.prompt: What could make public transport more attractive to use?
items.answer: Public transport would attract more users if it were cheaper, more frequent, and better connected, so that commuters saw it as a genuine alternative rather than a last resort.

title: Topic 13 · युवा, परिवार र पुस्तागत अन्तर
blocks: h2
Academic noun (१० वटा)
ul
**generation gap** (पुस्तागत अन्तर): The generation gap can strain family relationships.
**upbringing** (लालनपालन): A caring upbringing shapes a child’s character.
**adolescence** (किशोरावस्था): Adolescence is a period of rapid change.
**peer pressure** (साथीभाइको दबाब): Peer pressure influences teenage choices.
**nurture** (हेरचाह र पालनपोषण): Both nature and nurture shape personality.
**discipline** (अनुशासन): Consistent discipline helps children feel secure.
**household** (घरपरिवार): More households now have two working parents.
**sibling** (दाजुभाइ वा दिदीबहिनी): Sibling relationships influence social skills.
**autonomy** (आत्मनिर्भरता र स्वतन्त्रता): Teenagers increasingly demand greater autonomy.
**values** (मूल्य-मान्यता): Families pass on their core values.
h2
Precise verb (१० वटा) · past, participle, -ing रूप
ul
**nurture** (nurtured, nurtured, nurturing): Loving parents nurture confidence in their children.
**raise** (raised, raised, raising): It takes patience to raise a well-adjusted child.
**instil** (instilled, instilled, instilling): Schools instil discipline and respect.
**rebel** (rebelled, rebelled, rebelling): Teenagers sometimes rebel against strict rules.
**mature** (matured, matured, maturing): Children mature at different rates.
**bond** (bonded, bonded, bonding): Shared meals help families bond.
**influence** (influenced, influenced, influencing): Older siblings strongly influence younger ones.
**respect** (respected, respected, respecting): Children learn to respect others at home.
**neglect** (neglected, neglected, neglecting): Overworked parents may neglect family time.
**shape** (shaped, shaped, shaping): Early experiences shape lifelong attitudes.
h2
Collocation र adjective (१० वटा)
ul
**nuclear family**: The nuclear family is now the most common household. (Writing)
**extended family**: An extended family offers valuable support. (Speaking and Writing)
**peer pressure**: Peer pressure can lead teenagers astray. (Writing)
**work-life balance**: A healthy work-life balance benefits the whole family. (Writing)
**generation gap**: Technology has widened the generation gap. (Speaking and Writing)
**well-behaved**: Their children are remarkably well-behaved. (Speaking)
**close-knit**: We are a very close-knit family. (Speaking and Writing)
**parental guidance**: Young children need firm parental guidance. (Writing)
**role model**: Parents are a child’s first role model. (Speaking and Writing)
**quality time**: Busy parents should make time for quality time. (Speaking and Writing)
h2
Formal Task 2 collocation (५ वटा) · Writing
ul
**bridge the generation gap**: Open conversation can bridge the generation gap.
**instil moral values**: Families instil moral values in children.
**strike a balance between work and family**: Parents must strike a balance between work and family.
**shape a child’s character**: The early years shape a child’s character.
**spend quality time together**: Families should spend quality time together.
h2
Speaking idiom र expression (५ वटा) · Speaking-का लागि मात्र

**like father, like son**: He works in medicine too; like father, like son. (Part 3)
**bring up**: I was brought up by my grandparents. (Part 1)
**run in the family**: Musical talent runs in the family. (Part 1)
**see eye to eye**: Parents and teenagers do not always see eye to eye. (Part 3)

blocks.title: Exercise 4.13.3 · Speaking अभ्यास (Simulation Drill)
blocks.instructions: Part 3-को प्रत्येक question-को उत्तर २ देखि ३ वटा वाक्यमा दिनुहोस्, र कम्तीमा एउटा target idiom र एउटा collocation प्रयोग गर्नुहोस्। त्यसपछि model answer-सँग दाँजेर हेर्नुहोस्।

items.prompt: Do you think the generation gap is bigger today than in the past?
items.answer: The generation gap does feel wider today, largely because technology moves so fast that parents and teenagers do not always see eye to eye, though open conversation can still bridge it.

items.prompt: Who has more influence on children, parents or friends?
items.answer: Both matter, but as children grow, peer pressure often outweighs parental guidance; even so, parents remain the first role models and shape a child’s core values.

items.prompt: Is it better to grow up in a large family or a small one?
items.answer: There are trade-offs either way; a large family offers close-knit support, whereas a small one may allow more quality time and resources per child, so neither is simply better.

title: Topic 14 · वैज्ञानिक अनुसन्धान र नवप्रवर्तन
blocks: h2
Academic noun (१० वटा)
ul
**hypothesis** (परिकल्पना): A good hypothesis can be tested by experiment.
**breakthrough** (ठूलो नयाँ उपलब्धि): The vaccine was a major medical breakthrough.
**experimentation** (प्रयोग र परीक्षण): Careful experimentation drives scientific progress.
**innovation** (नवप्रवर्तन): Innovation depends on sustained investment.
**discovery** (खोज): The discovery changed our understanding of the brain.
**methodology** (अनुसन्धान विधि): A flawed methodology weakens any study.
**funding** (आर्थिक सहयोग): Research funding is fiercely competitive.
**peer review** (विज्ञहरूद्वारा गरिने समीक्षा): Peer review helps ensure reliable results.
**genetics** (वंशाणु विज्ञान): Advances in genetics raise new ethical questions.
**ethics** (नैतिकता): Research ethics protect human participants.
h2
Precise verb (१० वटा) · past, participle, -ing रूप
ul
**investigate** (investigated, investigated, investigating): Scientists investigate the causes of disease.
**discover** (discovered, discovered, discovering): Researchers discovered a new treatment.
**innovate** (innovated, innovated, innovating): Firms that innovate stay competitive.
**experiment** (experimented, experimented, experimenting): Teams experiment with cleaner materials.
**analyse** (analysed, analysed, analysing): Researchers analyse vast sets of data.
**hypothesise** (hypothesised, hypothesised, hypothesising): Scientists hypothesise before testing.
**fund** (funded, funded, funding): Governments fund basic research.
**validate** (validated, validated, validating): Repeated trials validate the findings.
**replicate** (replicated, replicated, replicating): Other labs must be able to replicate the results.

blocks.instructions: Part 3-को प्रत्येक question-को उत्तर २ देखि ३ वटा वाक्यमा दिनुहोस्, र कम्तीमा एउटा target idiom र एउटा collocation प्रयोग गर्नुहोस्। त्यसपछि model answer-सँग दाँजेर हेर्नुहोस्।

items.prompt: Should governments spend more money on scientific research?
items.answer: Governments should fund scientific research generously, because pushing the boundaries of knowledge through trial and error paves the way for the breakthroughs that improve everyday life.

items.prompt: Do you think all scientific progress is good for society?
items.answer: Not necessarily; while most research pushes the boundaries of knowledge for the better, some advances raise serious ethical questions, so progress needs to go hand in hand with careful regulation.

items.prompt: What recent invention has changed people’s lives the most?

**souvenir** (सम्झनाको चिनो): Tourists buy souvenirs to remember their trip.

**ecotourism** (पर्यावरणमैत्री पर्यटन): Ecotourism protects nature while creating jobs.

items.prompt: Why do you think international travel has become so popular?
items.answer: International travel has boomed because it broadens people’s horizons and offers a welcome change of scenery; once you catch the travel bug, exploring new destinations becomes hard to resist.

items.prompt: Does tourism do more good or harm to a country?
items.answer: It does both; tourism can boost the local economy and promote cultural understanding, yet mass tourism puts a strain on local resources and can degrade the very attractions people come to see.

items.prompt: Do you prefer package holidays or independent travel?
items.answer: I lean toward independent travel, because it lets you get off the beaten track and immerse yourself in local life, though a package holiday is more convenient if you are short on time.
